boundaries: `goToFrame`'s own inline comment (app.js:5145-5146: "Skipped during playback: goToFrame runs per displayed frame there") is STALE relative to the 2026-07 wall-clock-playback rewrite (CLAUDE.md §11-adjacent). Confirmed by direct read of `startPlay`/`playStep`/`advancePlayFrame` (timeline.js:17-125): playback advances via its OWN closure, `_advanceToFrame(next)` (timeline.js:71-83) — `saveAllLayerFrames();state.currentFrame=next;window._curFrame=next;` then a cache-blit or `loadFrame(next)`, then `updatePlayhead()` — a SEPARATE, independently-written duplicate of goToFrame's own save+advance+load+render sequence, not a call to `goToFrame` at all (confirmed by grep: zero `goToFrame(` occurrences inside `startPlay`'s own body). This scope's own `goToFrame` is therefore NEVER invoked by a genuine rAF playback tick; its three `!state.playing` guards (5148/5154/5173) only matter for a `goToFrame` call that happens to fire while `state.playing` is somehow already true from an UNRELATED caller (e.g. a script/API-driven `SM.frame=f`/`goToFrame(f)` call, nemo-script.js, mid-playback) — not for playback's own per-frame advance, contradicting the comment's own framing. Not fixed here (census scope only); flagged for a future pass — CLAUDE.md §3's warning about duplicated twin functions applies here in JS as much as it does to the Rust render()/render_to_pixels() pair it was written about.

`pushUndo(alreadySaved)` is a ONE-LINE ALIAS for `pushUndoLayers(alreadySaved)` (tweens.js:4741/4896, confirmed by direct read) — NOT a lighter, single-layer-scoped undo mechanism the name might suggest. Both take the SAME full `layersSnapshotNow()` snapshot, and both call `saveAllLayerFrames()` internally UNLESS their own `alreadySaved` argument is truthy. Across this scope's eight save/undo call sites the pattern is inconsistent: `insertKeyframe` (saveAllLayerFrames():5259, then bare pushUndoLayers():5272) and `insertKeyframeAt` (saveAllLayerFrames():5300, then bare pushUndoLayers():5304) each redundantly save all layers TWICE in a row; `convertToKeyframes` does the same in the OPPOSITE order (bare pushUndo():5379, which itself saves, immediately followed by an explicit `saveAllLayerFrames()` on the SAME line); `clearKeyframe` (pushUndo() alone:5344) and `removeTweenSpan` (pushUndo() alone:5361) and `insertFrame`/`removeFrame`/`removeFrameSpan` (bare pushUndoLayers() alone:5203/5325/5394) all rely SOLELY on the internal save, with no explicit call of their own. Only `insertBlankKeyframe` (saveAllLayerFrames():5313 then `pushUndoLayers(true)` on the SAME line) and the external caller select-bridge.js:1005-1011 (`saveAllLayerFrames(); pushUndoLayers(true);`, the wrapper around `_insertKeyframeCore`) pass `true` to suppress the redundant re-save — the only two call sites touching this scope's own functions that avoid it. Harmless (both save functions are idempotent replays over an already-consistent frame set — no data is lost or duplicated, only wall-clock wasted re-collecting every layer's strokes a second time), but not a pattern any comment in this scope is self-aware of. Not fixed here; flagged for a future pass.

`removeFrame` (app.js:5325-5336) and `removeFrameSpan` (app.js:5389-5400) splice content out of EVERY layer's `frames` array unconditionally, with NO `ld.locked` check anywhere in either function — confirmed by direct read (neither function references `.locked` at all). This is the OPPOSITE convention from three siblings in this same scope: `insertFrame`'s own explicit comment (5194-5200) states a locked layer must never get the real splice, only the harmless length-pad; `insertKeyframe`/`insertKeyframeAt` both explicitly skip `ld.locked&&!ld.symbolId` layers (5268/5302); and the external `cutFrames` (timeline.js:1802-1814, cited by line only) has its own explicit comment ("keep it in the clipboard..., just don't blank out a locked layer's own content") skipping the actual mutation for a locked layer while still recording it in the clipboard. `removeFrame`/`removeFrameSpan` instead delete a frame SLOT from a locked layer exactly like an unlocked one — arguably correct (removing a shared timeline column is a structural operation, not a content edit `editRefusalReason` would gate), but the asymmetry with `insertFrame`'s own explicit reasoning for the identical shared-column operation is not itself documented anywhere. Not fixed here; flagged for a future pass.

Contract item (c)'s own premise ("tweenMeta/pair data") does not correspond to any field in this codebase — confirmed by a whole-`src` grep for `tweenMeta`: zero hits anywhere. Tween pairs are never stored as metadata on a frame object; `removeTweenSpan`'s own two frame-index parameters (`fromF`/`toF`) are resolved by its caller from `tweenPairForCell` (timeline.js, cited by name only) at CLICK TIME by scanning forward/backward for the nearest bracketing keyframes, not read back from any persisted pair record. `removeTweenSpan` itself only ever mutates `f.strokes`/`f.isKeyframe`/`f.isInterpolated` on the frames strictly between the pair (5362-5365) — there is no separate pair-tracking structure to update or clear.

`convertToKeyframes`'s own guard (app.js:5381: `if(!f||f.isKeyframe)return;`) is BROADER than its own header comment implies. The comment (5369-5373) frames the feature as converting "a tweened inbetween, or content inherited from an earlier keyframe" into a real keyframe — but the guard only excludes frames that are ALREADY a keyframe; it does not require `f.isInterpolated` to be true. An ordinary, never-tweened HOLD frame (isKeyframe:false, isInterpolated:false, simply inheriting the previous keyframe's content per getEffectiveStrokes) is converted identically to a genuine tween inbetween — both end up with `f.isKeyframe=true;f.isInterpolated=false;count++` (5382). Not a bug (the header's own framing, "or content inherited from an earlier keyframe", already covers this case in prose even though the CODE comment block's own title emphasizes the tween case) — flagged only so a future reader doesn't assume the guard is narrower than it is.
